clue.text: Make unofficial attempt to stop lies broadcast through aerial

indicators.note: the inner group runs through the middle of the word for an aerial, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a dish is a satellite aerial

indicators.note: the attempt plugs a gap in the scrambled letters, as a stopper fills a hole
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of lies are spread into a new order

parts.note: a stab is an attempt, as in having a stab at something

explanation.surface: Someone tries to block lying propaganda being transmitted over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters come out as SELI, opened up to take the attempt. A dish is the bowl-shaped aerial for satellite television.
explanation.definitionFit: To disestablish a church is to strip it of its official, state-backed status.

clue.text: Mesdames in diamonds allure the most stupid

parts.note: D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the ladies is placed in the word for allure

parts.note: it is sex appeal or allure, as in a film star who has it
MMES is the standard French abbreviation for Mesdames

explanation.surface: French ladies dripping in jewels are said to be the dimmest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimmest is the superlative of dim, which is a colloquial synonym for stupid.

clue.text: US general sort of has men containing resistance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the resistance symbol inside them
to sort letters is to arrange them, so has men is put into a new order

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An American general's troops put up some opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges HAS MEN; 'containing' puts R inside to give SHERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tecumseh Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War.

clue.text: Quiet anger about writer's fluid waste allowance

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: the word for anger goes around the writing fluid

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
ink is the fluid a writer uses in a pen

explanation.surface: A furious author complains about how much ink is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is a retailer's term for stock lost to waste or theft, allowed for in accounts.

clue.text: Affected by fits, universal among the elderly

indicators.note: the letter for universal is placed among the letters for old people

parts.note: the aged are the elderly
U is the British film classification meaning universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Seizures are common among old people everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Agued describes someone stricken with ague, a fever marked by shivering fits.

clue.text: I'm all in, collapsing at a threshold

indicators.note: a collapsing structure falls into disorder, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted person falls down on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges the letters of I'M ALL IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Liminal comes from the Latin limen, a threshold, and describes being at a boundary.

clue.text: Medicine men offering bogus half-solution

parts.note: sham means bogus or fake

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for a solution is used

parts.note: an answer is the solution to a problem

explanation.surface: Healers sell a fake remedy that only half works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps ANS, the first three letters of ANSWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamans are spiritual healers in many traditional cultures, often called medicine men.

clue.text: Pipes outside greasy spoon on ancient support structures

indicators.note: the word for pipes goes around the rest

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice, so pipes means sings

indicators.note: in a down clue the cafe sits on top of the word for ancient

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe, a greasy spoon
old means ancient

explanation.surface: Plumbing runs around the outside of an old cafe under repair.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is the British slang spelling of cafe, used for cheap greasy-spoon eateries.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaffoldings are temporary frameworks of poles that support workers on buildings.

clue.text: American hopeful to secure games for social match?

indicators.note: the hopeful holds the games firmly inside

parts.note: a comer is American slang for an up-and-coming hopeful
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: An ambitious American signs up for sports to find a suitable partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is a companion or social equal, someone who is a match for you.

clue.text: Accidental in tune man dashed off

indicators.note: dashed off means written hastily and so jumbled, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A composer scribbles a melody without meaning to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed off' rearranges TUNE MAN; 'Accidental' tempts as a musical sharp or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmeant was not intended, so it happened by accident.

clue.text: Beadle's legal opinion: it's injurious to assist a whale

indicators.note: something injurious damages, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Helping a whale is said to be harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injurious' rearranges ASSIST A WHALE. Mr Bumble, the parish beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist, declares the law a fool in these words.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation is Mr Bumble the beadle's verdict on the law, an opinion about legality.

clue.text: Identify person who's in bondage losing head over one who isn't

indicators.note: over signals that the whole sequence is turned back to front

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a bonded person is dropped

parts.note: a serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land

explanation.surface: Picking out a slave who has been beheaded, as against a free citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A free person is the opposite of one in bondage, which is the sense of 'one who isn't'.

clue.text: Perhaps trumpeting has died for every fine space hero

indicators.note: for every says the swap of died for fine is made at each place it occurs, so both are changed
has here means the word takes on the letter for died in place of a letter for fine

parts.note: a fanfare is an example of trumpeting
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A trumpet flourish rings out for a dead hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has died for every fine' turns both Fs in FANFARE into D. Dan Dare was the pilot hero of the British comic Eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan Dare, Pilot of the Future, is a classic British science-fiction comic character.

clue.text: Had a meal in which starter is nothing like porridge

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is replaced by the letter for nothing

parts.note: eaten means had a meal
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone ate breakfast but the first course was nothing like porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaten means made of oats, as porridge is.

clue.text: An artist from Catalonia embracing America and a southern Spanish region

indicators.note: the painter's name wraps around the abbreviation for America

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a surrealist painter born in Catalonia

explanation.surface: A Catalan painter takes in an American and a region of southern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the autonomous community covering the south of Spain, including Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Thus puss in river is to dry out

indicators.note: the pair of words is placed in the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another on the English-Welsh border
sic is Latin for thus
puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat that falls into a river must be dried off.
explanation.definitionFit: To desiccate is to remove all moisture, to dry something out thoroughly.

clue.text: Buttonholes on opening?

parts.note: to buttonhole is to accost; reporters do this at a front door as it opens, standing on the steps

explanation.walkthrough: Buttonholes looks like a noun, holes for buttons, but it is a verb: accosts someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To doorstep someone is to accost them at their front door, as journalists do.

clue.text: Not surprisingly, damage to metalwork is accepted without question

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of the word are found in an unexpected order

parts.note: rust is the corrosion that damages iron and steel

explanation.surface: It is no surprise that corroded ironwork is taken as given.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something on trust is to accept it without checking or questioning it.

clue.text: Cod's cousins turned up, displacing a thousand shellfish

indicators.note: displacing means removing the letter for a thousand from the reversed word
in a down clue turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: pollacks are fish of the cod family
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Relatives of the cod turn up and push a thousand shellfish aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses POLLACKS to SKCALLOP; 'displacing' removes its K.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped shell, a common shellfish.

clue.text: Some of Tanzania's a major retreat for them

definitions.text: Some of Tanzania's a major retreat for them

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the run of letters is read right to left
some of means only part of the words is taken, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: Parts of Tanzania offer an important refuge for a people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' takes IASAM from TanzanIA'S A Major; 'retreat' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a semi-nomadic people of Kenya and northern Tanzania, whose land the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Old language of French revolutionary greeting

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical of the French Revolution
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary says hello in an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathi is an Indo-Aryan language of Maharashtra in India, with a long literary history.

clue.text: Southern European? Nothing new in that

definitions.text: Southern European? Nothing new in that

indicators.note: the zero score and the letter for new go inside the pair of letters from the first words

parts.note: love is nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A southern European? Nothing novel about that.
explanation.walkthrough: S and E from 'Southern European' wrap LOVE and N; the same two words also define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene, from Slovenia, is a European from the south of the continent.

clue.text: Buff brass lump attached to oak?

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a nut
brass means cheek or nerve, as gall does

explanation.surface: A lump of polished brass is fixed to an oak.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutgall is a growth formed on oak trees by gall wasps, a lump on the oak.

clue.text: Cleo and Brenda eclipsing every other girl's name

indicators.note: every other letter is blotted out, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Two women's names overshadow every other girl's.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiding the odd letters keeps LO from Cleo and RNA from Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a girl's name, popularised by Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Old-fashioned look adopted by traditionalist reduced sleaze

indicators.note: the look is taken into the shortened word for a conventional person
reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
lo is an archaic word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A stuffy conservative is seen to be squeezed by scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor is filth and sordidness, the kind of degradation sleaze means.

clue.text: Natural as an empty gallery

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a gallery with no paintings

explanation.definitionFit: Artless means simple and unaffected, and read in two parts it means lacking any art.

clue.text: Second best sheet newspaper cut for match supplement?

parts.note: top means best
a page is a sheet of paper
The Times, a British daily, cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: The second-best page of a newspaper is cut to make room for a sports supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppage time is extra time added at the end of a football match for interruptions.
